# Setnayan — Decision Log

> Split out of `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-06-03 to keep the auto-loaded primer light. **This file is NOT auto-loaded** — search it on demand, e.g. `grep -n "2026-06" DECISION_LOG.md`. **Append new rows at the bottom in date order**, format `| Date | Decision | Why-or-affected-files |`. The canonical primer + locked decisions live in `CLAUDE.md` (corpus root).

| 2026-05-09 | **0007 Budget & Expenses scope lock.** Three line items per vendor (Package, Crew Meal, Transportation), each with own deadline (couple-input in V1) and payment log. Payment records capture amount, date, method, reference, proof screenshot. Vendor's GCash/Maya/bank QR displayed per line for one-tap scan-to-pay (sourced from 0006). Rollup cards: total / paid / balance / next due. Calendar export via .ics (universal — Apple/Google/Outlook); default reminders 24h + 1h before deadline. Setnayan platform costs auto-populate from 0003 wallet (read-only). Misc free-form expenses supported. PHP only; no targets, no forecasting, no categories, no external sharing in V1. | User's stated goal was to curate every amount needing settlement — 3-line structure maps to actual Filipino vendor billing patterns. .ics over native EventKit/CalendarContract because no permissions/OAuth needed; works everywhere. Couple-only access matches existing wallet model. Targets/forecasting/multi-currency/sharing all V1.1+ candidates once we see usage data. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0007 calendar duplicate-avoidance — two layers.** Layer 1: stable VEVENT UIDs (`{event_id}-{line_item_id}@setnayan.ph`) so Apple/Google/Outlook update existing events on re-import instead of duplicating. Layer 2: per-line `tracked_in_calendar` boolean toggle. Bulk "Add all due dates" only exports lines flagged false; button text adapts ("Add 5 new dates" / "All on calendar — re-export?"). Couple manually toggles in either direction. | True calendar read access requires native app + permission OR OAuth per provider — V2 scope. The two-layer V1 approach gets ~95% of the value without the integration cost. UID dedup handles re-import duplicates automatically; manual flag handles cases where couple added to calendar outside Setnayan. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0010 Mood Board V1 — palettes only, Setnayan Guide rule engine.** Every guest-list role + venue gets a 6-color palette. Color input via hex / picker / name autocomplete (~300-entry library) / image extraction. 20 pre-template themes (Style: Classic/Pastel/Royalty/Nomadic/Sweet/Elegant/Dreamy/Muted/Boho · Color-led: Blue/Red/Green/Gold/Baby Blue/Army/Pink · Seasonal: Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter). Setnayan Guide rule engine evaluates 7 categories on every change: cohesion (8-color hard limit + 60-30-10 soft target), contrast (per-tier minimums + inversion check), background-vs-foreground proximity (ΔE 10), temperature consistency, saturation hierarchy, photography color cast, cultural defaults (PH bride white/ivory + sponsor pairing). Engine returns pass/warn/contradict states with structured suggestions. Disable toggle per-event (default ON) and per-palette ("Use this color anyway"). Master palette dedups by hex AND named color. Stylist persona, inspirations paste board, role outfit galleries, venue segments with photos/videos, concept-vs-actual all DEFERRED until stylist persona exists (V2 / Din). Saved palettes V1=couple-scoped, schema-ready for stylist scope V2. Mobile thumb-zone UX (all primary touch targets in lower third). | Engine baseline grounded in color theory + WCAG contrast ratios + wedding photography best practice + PH cultural conventions. Opinionated by design — couples save themselves photos that don't work. Override paths for couples who want full control. 20 themes parallel content workstream like 400 Reel templates and music catalogue; iteration code consumes via JSON manifest. Couple-scoped saved palettes today, stylist-scoped library lights up later when stylists exist (Din Phase 3). |

Balance + payment progress + overdue flag computed; surfaced in list and detail views. **Note:** 0007 Budget overlays this with a 3-line view (Package / Crew Meal / Transportation) for top-level budget UX; the underlying milestone schema in 0006 stays flexible. | PH wedding vendors structure schedules differently — fixed 3-stage forces couples to lie about reality. Schema flexibility costs little; UI presets keep entry fast for the common case. |

| 2026-05-09 | **0006 meetings module added to vendor profiles.** Each vendor has a list of scheduled meetings (initial consult, tasting, walkthrough, fitting, etc.) with title, datetime, mode (in-person/video/phone), location/link, agenda, attendees, post-meeting notes. Soonest upcoming surfaces as "Next meeting" on the vendor card; past-but-still-scheduled renders amber and prompts confirmation. `vendor_meetings` table includes a `created_by_actor` column ('couple' in V1) so Din (Phase 3) can later write 'vendor' rows into the same table without migration. | 2026-05-09 | **0008 Seating Chart table catalog locked at 13 entries.** Round (8/10/12), Long banquet (6/8/10), Family head — long rectangular (12/14/16), Sweetheart (2), Serpentine (10/14/18). Family head tables are explicitly **long rectangulars, not ovals** — sized larger than the standard long banquet and reserved for the immediate family of the bride or groom. Capacity is bound to type — no per-table custom-capacity in V1. Custom shapes deferred to V1.1. | Covers 95%+ of Filipino reception venues. Avoids the rabbit hole of arbitrary geometry; serpentine added explicitly because Filipino entourage tables often use it; family-head ovals were a visual mistake — Filipino venues stock these as long banquet tables, not oval tops. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 floor plan carries full venue elements**, not just tables. Stage is required; band platform is optional (adjacent to or on the stage); dancefloor is an optional rectangle in front of the stage that no tables may sit inside; at least one main entrance door is required by Publish (side / service doors optional). Doors snap to walls only and render as arched gaps in the wall line. | The seating chart is the canonical reception layout, used by Print pack signs and by Paparazzi (0012) for orientation. Modeling stage / band / dancefloor / doors as first-class elements means the print-pack overview reads as a real floor plan rather than just a table grid. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 venue dimensions are optional.** Couples who already know their venue size flip a toolbar toggle to set room width × length in metres; the editor then renders walls at scale and bounds placement (no tables outside walls, on doors, or on the dancefloor). Couples who don't know yet leave it blank — placement is fully free-form, the canvas grows to fit content, no walls are drawn. Couples can set or clear at any time. | Forcing dimensions upfront would block planning for couples who book the venue but haven't measured it. Free-form is the early-planning default; bounded mode is a precision affordance for the home stretch. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 rotation rule by shape.** Round, sweetheart, family-head: rotation locked at 0°. Long banquet (`long_*`) and serpentine (`serpentine_*`): rotation in **45° increments** (0/45/90/135/180/225/270/315). | Filipino venues are rarely orthogonal — couples need 45° steps to align friend / entourage tables to non-orthogonal walls and aisles. Round and sweetheart don't benefit from rotation; family-head tables sit perpendicular to the stage by convention. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 alignment lock on by default.** Dragging a table reveals pink horizontal and vertical guide lines that snap the moving table's center, top edge, or left edge to the same coordinate as nearby stationary tables. Toggleable in the toolbar; complementary to (not a replacement for) the 10-pt grid snap. | Without alignment guides, a 60-table reception ends up with subtle misalignments that look bad in the printed overview. Lock-on-default mirrors how Figma / Sketch behave; couples turn it off only for pixel-precise edge cases. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 chair-level interaction.** Every table renders chairs as small circles around the perimeter — one per seat. Filled with profile photo when available; with two-letter initials on a side-coded gradient when not. Empty seats render dashed-outline white. **Gestures:** tap chair = swap that guest's seat (single-seat move); long-press chair = open guest details; tap table body = swap that whole table's position with another (everyone seated stays with their table); long-press table = table settings. Initials-only chairs surface the full name on selection via a floating name pop and a sticky banner at the top of the canvas. | The chair-circle model mirrors how couples actually think about seating — by person, not by abstract slot. Splitting tap (swap) from long-press (details) keeps the primary interaction (move someone to a different seat) one-handed and fast. The dual hit-zone (chair circles vs. table body) lets a single tap gesture mean two different things without a mode switch. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 serpentine geometry locked.** A serpentine segment is a quarter-donut wedge — one quarter of a ring — with **2 inner-cove chairs + 4 outer-edge chairs = 6 seats per segment**. Couples assemble multiple segments into C-shapes, U-cups, and longer arcs. Catalog ships 1/2/3-segment configurations (`serpentine_6` / `serpentine_12` / `serpentine_18` = 6/12/18 seats). Serpentines are **resizable in place** via the table-detail sheet — adding or removing a segment without deleting and re-creating the table; capacity = `6 × segments`. Earlier representations (S-curve strokes, line-only paths) were wrong — serpentines are real banded tables with width, fillet, and chairs on both inside and outside. | Matches reference photos of real Filipino-wedding entourage tables. The 2+4 chair pattern is dictated by the donut geometry: the inner arc is shorter, fits ~2; the outer arc is longer, fits ~4. Locking this prevents future "let's make it 5 chairs" drift, and the segment-based capacity makes the resize affordance trivial to spec. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 stage placement is free anywhere on the canvas.** Top, bottom, left, right edge, or true center for in-the-round receptions. Auto-fill ring distances recompute around wherever the stage lands. | Real Filipino venues run all four orientations plus the occasional in-the-round. Locking the stage to one edge would force couples to mentally rotate every venue into our model. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 auto-fill uses role-tier rings centered on the stage.** Tier 1 (principal sponsors + officiant + immediate family) innermost; Tier 2 (entourage + secondary sponsors + bearers + flower girl) second; Tier 3 (extended family) third; Tier 4 (friends, work, school) outermost. Sweetheart tables are excluded from the rotation. Locked tables are skipped. Already-placed guests are never moved. | Matches how Filipino weddings actually seat people. Family-side L/R splits and mobility-first heuristics were considered and deferred — V1 ships the dominant strategy. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 table QR tokens are minted only at Publish, never on draft.** Print pack download unlocks at publish; re-publish is idempotent (existing tokens unchanged, new tables get fresh tokens). | Avoids QR churn while couples plan. Print pack is the offline event-day artifact; once minted, tokens travel with the printed signs. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Peer guest-to-guest tagging is QR-scan only.** No roster/list view inside the gallery for picking a friend. The only path to tag another guest is to physically scan that guest's personal QR (printed on their place card from 0008's print pack). Table-sign QR auto-tags everyone seated at that table (capped at the existing 10-tag-per-photo limit). | Privacy-first by default — no browseable guest directory. Presence at the venue is the consent gate for tagging. Removes the surveillance affordance of "search the wedding for someone you fancy" while preserving the social affordance of "tag your friend in the photo we just took." |
| 2026-05-09 | **Tag-once trust handshake.** Scanning a guest's personal QR is a one-time consent gesture per pair. Once A has scanned B's QR once, A is added to B's `tag_consent_grantees` set and may tag B in any of A's own future photos for the rest of the event without rescanning. The relationship is one-way (A→B) and event-scoped. | Removes the friction of repeatedly scanning a friend you're already shooting all evening, while preserving the consent gate established by the first scan. Revocation flow (per-grantee opt-out) deferred to V1.1; V1 only offers the global photo_consent toggle as a kill-switch. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Voice/video guestbook is part of Wedding Challenges, not a standalone iteration.** When the Wedding Challenges iteration is drafted, it must include the guestbook surface (voice or video recording up to 60 seconds, in-app prompts like "Share a memory," "Give your wishes," "Tell them a secret") as one of its challenge types. | The blueprint lists guestbook as a top-line guest feature, but conceptually it's a "prompt → recording → submission" loop — exactly what a Challenges system already does. Folding it in keeps the platform leaner and gives every challenge the same plumbing (prompt, capture, submit, gallery). |
| 2026-05-09 | **Coordinator surfaces deferred from V1.** The blueprint's coordinator-facing cluster (web QR scanning station, multi-staff PIN access, three scanning modes, real-time arrival count, broadcast notifications, dietary tracker, encrypted local data bundle, thermal label printer support, geo-tag arrival, post-event PDF) is **out of V1 scope**. Vendor list (already in 0006) is the only coordinator surface that ships in V1. The coordinator app cluster is a future phase. | V1 is already large; coordinators are a power-user tier whose absence doesn't block couples or guests from using the product. Vendor list covers the most common coordinator need (calling vendors). The full coordinator cluster ships when V1 has launch data and the coordinator persona's actual workflow is observed. |
| 2026-05-09 | **30-day post-download compression rule.** When a couple or guest downloads the originals of any photo (or full album), the source file in Setnayan's storage is auto-compressed 30 days after the download timestamp. The compressed copy replaces the original on R2; the file remains visible to the user but only in compressed form going forward. The 30-day grace gives the user time to verify the download succeeded before Setnayan's bandwidth/storage cost is reduced. | Cost-management rule. Once the user holds the originals, Setnayan doesn't need to keep paying for hot-tier original storage. Compressing instead of deleting preserves the user's gallery view and re-share capability. The 30-day grace prevents accidental loss if the download was corrupted or lost. **Applies to:** 0009 Photo Delivery, 0012 Paparazzi gallery, 0010 Mood Board, any future photo-bearing iteration. **Does NOT apply to:** files the user has not downloaded — those follow the standard tier-retention windows (hot 90 days → IA cold 5 years for paparazzi). |
| 2026-05-09 | **Push/SMS/email fallback channels deferred from V1.** Notifications are in-UI only across all V1 iterations (vendor deadlines, meeting reminders, RSVP nudges, etc.). The blueprint's promised push (FCM/APNs), SMS fallback, and email fallback all ship in a later iteration. | Each channel adds compliance, deliverability, and per-message cost overhead. V1 ships in-UI surfacing across every iteration that needs it; the dedicated notifications iteration owns the multi-channel layer when we're ready to absorb the operational cost. Until then, "fallback" copy in any spec or mockup must be removed or downgraded to "future." |
| 2026-05-09 | **Apparatus-only pricing rule sharpened.** Every Setnayan SKU prices the Setnayan software TOOL or SERVICE the couple unlocks — never the hardware they shoot on, never the people who operate it, never the hours they use it. "Apparatus" = seats / app-access counts, capability unlocks (templates, Pro widgets, custom monogram pack), service / kit access. NOT apparatus = phone hardware, tripods/lavaliers/mics (those are sold as separate optional kits if at all), human crew of any kind, hours of coverage, ingest minutes, event duration. Couples bring their own phones and recruit their own operators. | Stated by user as "we are only charging for the apparatus" then sharpened to "the phone is not included, the crew is not included — we are only providing the tool that can make this work." Makes Setnayan's product model consistent across every iteration. Exposes Live Stream Tiers 5–8 (crew-bundled) as the outlier — those get cut from V1. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Live Stream V1 — apparatus pricing + 4-tier lineup + YouTube-only delivery.** Cuts Tiers 5–8 from V1 (crew bundles violate apparatus rule). Reprices Tier 1–4 to clean × 30 token math: ₱4,500 / ₱7,500 / ₱5,000 / ₱9,000. Drops the ₱999 Wedding Ceremony +3 hrs add-on (sold hours, violates rule). Drops the standalone ₱499 Facebook Live add-on (folded into Tier 4). Coverage on every tier = the couple's full event window; no hour gates. | Aligns Live Stream with the apparatus rule. Couples pay for the camera-slot count + capability set, get the tool for as long as their wedding lasts. The crew-bundled tiers may revive as a future "Setnayan Pro Services" line of business but are explicitly NOT a Setnayan software platform SKU. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Live Stream V1 — pivot to base + add-ons, drop Native track entirely.** Replaces the 4-tier lineup with a single base SKU (`live_stream_base`, ₱2,500 — 1 broadcaster + 3 cameras + 3 hours of stream capacity) plus two capacity add-ons (`live_stream_camera_addon` ₱1,000, max +2; `live_stream_hour_addon` ₱1,000, unlimited). Native iOS/Android camera-operator apps DROPPED from V1 entirely — V1 is pure WebApp + YouTube delivery. Apparatus rule reframed: "hours of stream capacity" counts as apparatus (it's a finite computational resource Setnayan's infrastructure provides), distinct from "hours of crew coverage" (which is labor). Clean × 30 token math, all 999 prices rounded to clean integers. | Base + add-ons aligns Setnayan's revenue with actual cost (Cloudflare ingest scales per camera-hour). Couples streaming a short ceremony pay ₱2,500 entry; couples broadcasting a full day pay proportionally. Margin holds at ~95% across the entire range. Native track was speculative future-V2 scope; cutting clarifies V1 ships pure WebApp. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Live Stream V1 — Broadcast Style Pack + AI Edited Highlight + free polish features.** New ₱3,000 add-on (`broadcast_style_pack`) bundles all four broadcast style modes (News, Cinematic, Sports, Royalty), all transition types (crossfade, slide, push, iris reveal), four color presets per mode, and animated scene cards. Broadcaster can switch styles mid-event. New ₱5,000 add-on (`ai_edited_highlight`, multi-purchase) — 3-minute themed multi-segment polished reel from broadcast clips + paparazzi photos; auto-inherits Broadcast Style if owned. Free in base SKU: highlight markers (★ button on broadcaster admin), Cast to projector (laptop HDMI for full polished composite, iPhone HDMI for raw active feed via iOS fullscreen-video routing). Cross-iteration integration: when LED Background (0005) + Custom Monogram Pack (0011) both owned, 1080p LED render becomes the standby video. Same-Day Edit deferred from V1 — vision AI cost (~₱9,500/event realistic) too high; revisit V1.1 once costs drop. | All new add-ons are pure software margin (~99%). The bundled style pack is simpler for couples than 4 separate ₱3,000 SKUs and gives mid-event mode switching for free. The free base features (highlight markers + projector cast) make Setnayan's Live Stream feel complete out of the box without forcing every polish behind a paywall. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Live Stream delivers exclusively via YouTube.** YouTube is the sole viewer-delivery surface in V1. | 2026-05-14 | **Caching & Offline Strategy locked.** Hard 100 MB per-user/per-install storage budget gated by `navigator.storage.estimate()` at startup (drops to 50% of available headroom if browser reports < 100 MB free). Allocation: ~75 MB images · ~20 MB JSON/data · ~5 MB headroom; splits soft, LRU within each layer. Two-layer architecture: (1) **Data layer** = TanStack Query + `persistQueryClient` to IndexedDB with stale-while-revalidate, per-query TTL, hard `maxAge` (7 days), and `buster` key bumped per schema change; (2) **Asset layer** = service worker (`apps/web/public/sw.js`) with route-scoped `CacheExpiration` (`maxEntries` + `maxAgeSeconds`) for images (500 entries / 30 days), JS chunks (100 entries / 7 days, stale-while-revalidate), fonts (20 entries / 1 year). **MUST cache:** app shell, JS chunks, fonts, public-read data (events, guests, vendor profiles, mood board, schedule, budget, save-the-date assets). **MUST NEVER cache:** auth tokens, Supabase session, payment intents, BIR receipts, contract files, API-gateway per-request-key responses, live chat (use Realtime). **Invalidation discipline:** every mutation MUST invalidate its query key — enforced via `useTrackedMutation` wrapper around `useMutation` with required `invalidates: QueryKey[]` field + ESLint rule `setnayan/no-raw-mutation` blocking raw `useMutation` in feature code. **Stale-time defaults** (overridable per query): hot lists (guests, day-of schedule) 60s · warm data (vendor profiles, mood board, budget) 5min · cold/immutable (BIR receipts, finalized themes) 1hr. **Eviction:** LRU per layer (assets by `lastAccessedAt`, data by `dataUpdatedAt`); no cross-layer fallback. **Out of scope:** native iOS/Android offline (Phase 2) · photo gallery archive downloads (0009 handles via direct R2 signed URLs + native share, not the PWA cache) · music catalogue files (R2 HTTP cache, not service worker). Canonical spec at `02_Specifications/Caching_and_Offline_Strategy.md`. Acceptance criteria for Sprint 0 validation: cold visit <1.5s on 4G (Lighthouse mobile) · warm return renders cached guest list <100ms before revalidation · quota-hit LRU verified by programmatic 75 MB fill test · schema buster wipes persisted blob on bump · ESLint rule blocks merge on raw `useMutation` · automated audit asserts no auth/payment/receipt/contract content in IndexedDB or SW caches · 200-guest day-of stress test bounds network with 60s staleTime. | Solves two predictable failure modes for return visits to a planning-tool app couples will use over 6–18 months: (1) cold start latency — returning users opening their dashboard shouldn't wait on network to see their guest list, they should see the last-known state in <100ms with background revalidation; (2) unbounded storage bloat — a user who has accumulated a year of vendor portraits, mood-board thumbs, and save-the-date previews shouldn't end up with 500 MB of Setnayan assets eating device storage. Two-layer split keeps eviction reasoning local — image churn doesn't pressure the data cache and vice versa. Sensitive data exclusion (auth, payment intents, BIR receipts, contracts) is non-negotiable for PH legal compliance + RA 10173. Mutation-invalidation wrapper makes the discipline impossible to bypass, which matters because cache-related bugs are notoriously hard to diagnose in production — surfacing them at lint time prevents shipping them. Strategic intent is to make Setnayan the most accessible Filipino events platform across every device surface a couple or vendor might pick up — laptop on Sunday afternoon planning, phone for guest-list edits in transit, tablet for venue walkthroughs, desktop for vendor calendar management. Native apps also unlock OS-level integrations (file system, reliable push, deep-link handlers) PWA installs can't fully deliver — especially relevant for vendor desktop workflows (calendar sync · proposals · contracts). Label stays "Create account" — only destination changes; Next.js `usePathname()` in shared header. | Three drivers. **First**, the brief had been accumulating quickly across this single session (multi-platform expansion · "no one else comes close" positioning · stats section · dropped pricing on public site) and owner asked for external research grounding before locking content. Cream base (`#FAF6F0`), ink (`#1A1A1A`), and the Manrope-body / Cormorant-italic-display / DM-Mono editorial typography stack from the prior Setnayan Default are preserved. Icon stroke remains 1.75. Schema CHECK constraint key `'setnayan_default'` is unchanged — no rename, no migration needed. Reconciled with 0015's "no competing accents" discipline by limiting Default to a single burgundy accent — no secondary gold/sage. Previous terracotta tokens (`#C97B4B / #8C4A28 / #E8C9B0`) retired from the default; admin can re-seed terracotta as a custom theme via `brand_config_versions` if desired. **(b) New fifth UI Theme: "Forest Theme" (`[data-theme="forest_theme"]`).** Vendor-grounded / professional register distinct from the romantic register of Default. Tokens: `--page-bg: #F4F0E8` (warm off-cream with subtle green cast), `--surface: #FFFFFF`, `--ink: #1A2520`, `--ink-soft: #5C6660`, `--accent: #2D4A3A` (deep forest — trust, calm, grounds vendor / contract / payment surfaces), `--accent-deep: #1A2F23`, `--accent-soft: #B8C9BF`, `--gold: #C9A66B` (reuses Victorian's existing `--gold` token for a single platform-wide champagne value). Body: Manrope 400/500/600 · Display: Cormorant Garamond italic 500 · Mono: DM Mono 400 (matches editorial restraint of Default, not Victorian's ornate Playfair register). Icon stroke: 1.75. Page-level accent is always forest; gold is constrained to existing tint roles already speced in 0015 § Section 8 (Boosted-vendor gradient · Certified-vendor badge · celebration-affordance moments) — preserves "no competing accents at the page level" discipline. **(c) Public marketing site palette (0015 § Voice) now inherits accent from primary admin's active UI Theme via `brand_config_versions`** (already speced in 0023 § 3.7 for color tokens with two-admin approval per § 9.1). Previously 0015 L151 locked a fixed terracotta accent; that hard-coded accent is replaced with admin-controlled token inheritance, with **Setnayan Default as the seed default**. The platform admin (iteration 0023, NOT couple admin or vendor admin) selects one of the five UI Themes as the platform's brand-active theme; the marketing site reads `brand_config_versions.active_theme_id` and applies the corresponding accent. New customer / vendor accounts without a personal `users.theme_preference` selection inherit the platform's brand-active theme on first dashboard load. **Overlap acknowledged but not collapsed.** Victorian (burgundy `#8B1E3F` + gold leaf + ornate Playfair + flourishes — Bridgerton / heritage) and Setnayan Default (burgundy `#7A1F2B` + modern editorial Cormorant — Aesop / Aman register) share the burgundy color family but are distinguished by hex (one shade deeper / cooler), typography (Playfair 700 italic vs Cormorant italic 500), gold-leaf secondary (Victorian-only), icon stroke (2.25 vs 1.75), and intent (heritage-formal vs modern brand baseline). Classy (`#B8945F` champagne primary) and Forest Theme (`#C9A66B` champagne as constrained secondary tint on forest primary) share the champagne family but differ in base color, typography (Cinzel display vs Cormorant italic), and gold-as-primary vs gold-as-tint role. **Outstanding pre-existing drift partially addressed:** COWORK.md L127 previously listed the fourth theme as "Modern Minimalist" (corpus inconsistency with Theme System Implementation Spec / 0025 schema / Installed_Stack_Inventory all of which name it "iOS"); this edit pass corrects COWORK.md to "iOS" while restating the five themes — flagged as part of this lock rather than deferred to a separate cleanup. | Reconciles owner directive ("make this our default color · burgundy and cream only · forest with champagne gold as another") with the 0015 "no competing accents" editorial discipline and the existing 4-theme system without exploding the surface. Burgundy reads "this is serious / committed" and lands the wedding/life-events emotional register without the saccharine pink default that haunts most wedding-tech UX; forest grounds the planning-anxiety temperature on vendor-side surfaces; cream evokes paper invitations / abaca / lace — premium-Filipino texture rather than sterile SaaS. Default keeping modern editorial typography while Victorian keeps ornate Bridgerton typography preserves the "five distinct theme intents" goal — two themes sharing burgundy doesn't reduce choice if their typography and gold-leaf treatment land in different aesthetic worlds. The five themes now span: modern editorial brand baseline (Default) · heritage-formal Bridgerton (Victorian) · understated champagne luxury (Classy) · system-native iOS (iOS) · vendor-grounded forest + gold (Forest Theme). Wiring the public website palette to the primary admin's setting via `brand_config_versions` unifies aesthetic governance — admin already owns logo / wordmark / tagline / color tokens via 0023 § 3.7 — instead of forking website-palette decisions into a separate edit surface. Two-admin approval gate already applies to brand-mark changes per 0023 § 9.1; the spec extension makes UI Theme switches at the platform level subject to the same gate (the gate did not previously cover theme switches because the public-site palette was hard-coded). | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); | 2026-05-15 | **Vendor public-visibility state machine + Website editor widget architecture (locked).** Two coupled decisions extending the morning's stack. **(1) Vendor public-visibility correction.** Vendors who have registered but are not yet verified now show on the public marketplace as **"Coming soon"** cards instead of being hidden. New column `vendors.public_visibility ENUM('hidden','coming_soon','verified','archived') DEFAULT 'coming_soon'` (iteration 0022 § 2.1c). States: `coming_soon` (default at registration · profile publicly listed with muted "Coming soon" badge · no booking CTA · read-only preview) → `verified` (set by admin via Verification Queues 0023 § 3.2 · fully bookable) · `hidden` (admin suspension / withdrawal · not surfaced anywhere) · `archived` (terminal · removed from browse · existing relationships preserve referential integrity). DIY-mode marketplace browse popup (0006 § DIY-mode filter popup) gains a **"Verified only"** toggle OFF by default — couples see both states; toggle ON filters to verified-only. **`verified_vendor_count` metric** (Section 3 stats threshold + Section 1 announcement bar auto-hide + boost-service launch gate 2026-05-14) continues to count only `public_visibility='verified'` rows; `coming_soon` vendors are visible publicly but do NOT contribute to the verification-count threshold metrics. State transitions are audit-logged in `admin_audit_log` (action `vendor_visibility_change`). **(2) Widget architecture refactor + admin Website editor (iteration 0023 § 3.10 = 8th admin surface).** The 12 marketing-site sections in 0015 are generalized as widgets in a registry table `site_widgets (widget_id PK, page, display_order, is_enabled, gate_type, config JSONB, updated_at, updated_by_admin_id)`. Page-scoped (`home` · `for_vendors` · `features` · `about` — extensible). Three gate types: `NULL` (always-on widget) · `'count'` (gated by count thresholds — Section 3 stats) · `'per_tile'` (per-tile visibility — Section 12 platforms). **V1 admin-editable fields:** `is_enabled` + `display_order` ONLY. Per-widget config (stats thresholds · platform store URLs · copy overrides · A/B variants) stays code-locked in V1; admin editing of `config` JSONB deferred to V1.1. **Admin Website editor surface at `/admin/website`** (iteration 0023 § 3.10) — list of widgets per page · drag-drop reorder · enable/disable toggle · audit-logged via `admin_audit_log` actions `site_widgets_toggle` / `site_widgets_reorder` · single-admin authority per § 4.3 · mobile lives under "More" tab. **Iteration 0023 admin surface count 7 → 8** (§ 1 table extended with new row 8). **Replaces** the standalone `site_visibility_flags` table from the morning's stats-gating entry — folded into `site_widgets.is_enabled` + the derived `count_gate_passes` check on `gate_type='count'` widgets. `platform_availability` table (Section 12 per-tile detail) stays as sibling table linked logically to `home_platforms` widget by convention. | Two drivers. **First**, the vendor `public_visibility` default shift from `hidden` → `coming_soon` addresses the chicken-and-egg problem of a launching marketplace: pre-verification vendors who completed registration but haven't yet been admin-reviewed need somewhere to land that's neither "fully bookable" nor "invisible." A "Coming soon" surface state lets couples see real coverage forming on the marketplace before the verified vendor pool reaches critical mass, while honestly signaling that the vendor isn't yet bookable. Honest-but-visible beats hidden-until-perfect for two reasons: couples gain confidence the platform is growing; vendors are incentivized to complete verification quickly to flip status. The `verified` count metrics (Section 3 stats gate, announcement bar auto-hide, boost-service launch gate) stay strict — `coming_soon` vendors don't count toward thresholds — so trust signals remain honest. **Second**, the widget architecture refactor was already implicit in the morning's per-section gating tables (`site_visibility_flags` for Section 3, `platform_availability` for Section 12); generalizing it to all 12 sections gives admins a single place to manage marketing-site composition without separate per-section toggles in code. Limiting V1 admin scope to `is_enabled` + `display_order` (not config / copy / variants) keeps the editor surface tight while solving the immediate need (turn sections off when they're not yet relevant; reorder for A/B if needed). The decision NOT to support per-widget config editing in V1 is deliberate — keeping the iteration spec as the source of truth for content means engineering doesn't have to build a "marketing CMS" that competes with spec authority. | 2026-05-16 | **Monogram Hero PNG-to-SVG conversion via Potrace · amends earlier SVG-only-hard-block stance.** Second 2026-05-16 row, amendment to the first. The earlier entry's *"PNG monogram uploads rejected at upload time for the Monogram Hero upgrade"* hard block is **softened** to a **hybrid policy with preview gate**: PNG uploads are accepted, server-side Potrace conversion runs, the couple sees a preview of the converted SVG + trace animation, and the couple explicitly approves the converted version before checkout proceeds. **Locked flow (6 steps):** (1) Couple in Monogram Hero checkout, has PNG monogram. (2) Editor offers "Convert your PNG to SVG so it can animate? We'll show you the result first." (3) Couple taps Convert → server runs Potrace via Cloudflare Worker (WASM build) → ~2 second wait. (4) Preview screen: side-by-side original PNG + animated SVG trace preview (looping ~3s). (5) Three CTAs: **Use this SVG · Try a different file · Use auto-generated instead**. (6) On *Use this SVG*: checkout proceeds with the converted SVG stored as canonical (`hero_monogram.converted_svg_url`); **PNG original kept as backup** under `hero_monogram.uploaded_url` for audit / archive / future re-conversion if Potrace settings improve. **Engine choice: Potrace (open-source).** Wrapped as a Cloudflare Worker WASM function. Free per conversion (~₱0 marginal cost). Mature, battle-tested (Inkscape's Trace Bitmap is built on it). Quality 80–90% on high-contrast monogram-style content. Alternatives considered + rejected: Vectorizer.ai API (~₱11/conversion, vendor lock-in), ImageTracerJS (lower quality), Adobe Image Trace API (overkill + expensive). **No-refund clause still stands** for the Monogram Hero SKU — the preview gate IS the consent mechanism (couple sees exactly what they're paying for before commit), so all-sales-final remains morally defensible. **Schema additions to `hero_monogram.config_json`:** `converted_svg_url` (R2 path to Potrace output), `converted_svg_approved_at` (ISO timestamp of couple's preview-gate approval), `converted_svg_potrace_settings` (threshold / turdsize / optcurve / opttolerance — captured for reproducibility if we re-run conversion with improved defaults). **API integration:** Potrace WASM build deployed as a Cloudflare Worker function (`/api/monogram/convert`); reads PNG from R2 `setnayan-media`, writes SVG to same bucket under `hero_monogram/{event_id}/converted.svg`, returns preview-renderable URL. Engineering effort ~3 days (Potrace WASM compile + Worker wiring + preview-gate UI in the upgrade flow + acceptance approval write to schema). | The earlier hard-block was the right *default* but unnecessarily restrictive on what is technically possible. Many couples receive their monogram as PNG from their wedding-branding designer (the designer keeps the SVG source); forcing those couples to either (a) go back to the designer for SVG, (b) use auto-generated instead, or (c) skip the ₱1,999 upgrade entirely all leak conversion. The preview gate protects the quality bar without locking out couples who only have PNG — they self-select away from bad conversions because they see the result before paying. Potrace specifically (vs the commercial alternatives) keeps marginal cost at ₱0, which protects the 95%+ margin on the ₱1,999 SKU. The 10% of conversions that look mediocre will be revealed at the preview gate and rejected by the couple before payment; the no-refund clause therefore stays clean. PNG-as-backup is a low-cost safety net (PNG is small; R2 storage cost negligible) that enables future re-conversion if we improve Potrace settings or add a better engine in V1.1+. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0004_invitation_widgets/0004_invitation_widgets.md` (`hero_monogram` schema extended with conversion fields; Monogram Hero purchase flow rewritten to surface the 6-step preview-gate path instead of the SVG-required hard-block; the earlier *"SVG-only: PNG monogram uploads rejected at upload time"* line replaced with the hybrid policy; acceptance criteria updated to test the conversion + preview-approval flow); `API_Integration_Checklist.md` (new Tier 5 entry — Potrace WASM build + Cloudflare Worker deploy + R2 routing); ~~`0002_qr_invitation_system/0002_qr_invitation_system.md`~~ no edit needed (mentions "SVG-only" only in passing reference to 0004's rules). **`.docx` mirrors NOT regenerated** (pandoc unavailable). **Engineering implementation pending** — Potrace WASM compile (npm `potrace-wasm` exists; verify size + license); Cloudflare Worker `/api/monogram/convert` endpoint; preview-gate UI component in the Monogram Hero checkout step (side-by-side PNG vs animated SVG trace); schema migration for the 3 new `hero_monogram` config fields. **Sequencing note:** Amends the first 2026-05-16 row's *"SVG-only no fallback"* line; both rows together describe the final V1 Monogram Hero policy. |

AI Video Highlight (₱999/60s) and AI Edited Highlight (₱2,999/3min) similarly consume the couple's YouTube archive. **Day-of-build engineering surface drops by ~60%** — no Cloudflare Stream Live ingest, no SFU subscription, no server-side ffmpeg compositor with monogram overlay, no RTMP relay to a master Setnayan channel; broadcaster web UI + landing-page IFrame embed are the entire V1 build. | Three drivers. **First**, composite costs were the largest variable-cost line in the Panood economics: Cloudflare Stream Live ingest at ~$1 per 1,000 minutes per camera (5 cams × 5 hrs × 60min = 1,500 minutes × ~₱60 = ~₱90 per typical event), plus server-side ffmpeg compositor compute, plus RTMP relay. Pushing the composite to YouTube (where it is free at unbounded scale) and shifting Setnayan's role to broadcaster orchestration drops the variable cost line to near zero. **Second**, the couple-owns-the-video model resolves a long-standing tension around "what happens when Setnayan eventually wraps or rebrands or rotates the @SetnayanWeddings channel?" — by storing the video on the couple's own YouTube, the broadcast is durable independent of Setnayan's platform lifecycle. **Third**, per-day pricing aligns with how couples actually plan multi-day Filipino weddings (prep day + ceremony + reception are often 3 distinct days at distinct venues); buying coverage day-by-day is more honest than a 3-hour base + hour-addons model that mismatches a 2-day or 3-day event. The Annual SKUs (₱2,999 / ₱3,999) open a vendor-side ARR line — vendors who livestream their own portfolio events year-round have a single-purchase option that's break-even after ~6 days/year of use. **Tax-tier note:** Daily Broadcast nets ~67-72% margin under V1 tax tier; The retired SKU was a "render the landing-page hero into 3 video aspect ratios" feature; this is "AI-edit 5-10 engagement photos into one social-share clip" — fundamentally different inputs, fundamentally different outputs, different engineering pipelines. | 2026-05-16 | **Patiktok V1 SKU lock — dual-tier (Setnayan TikTok ₱999/day vs Personal TikTok ₱1,999/day) · 40-video soft cap per booth per day · ₱49/+10 overage · per-day multi-purchase.** Sixth 2026-05-16 row. Patiktok pricing model **replaces** the prior single-SKU ₱2,499/booth/5hr model (and its ₱999 additional-station + ₱499/hour add-on tier) with a **dual-tier per-day** model based on **who owns the videos**. **(1) Setnayan TikTok tier — ₱999/day:** videos auto-post to **Setnayan's master TikTok handle `@SetnayanWeddings`** (or similar); Setnayan retains ad-revenue upside if the compilation goes viral; couple gets the post link + downloadable MP4 with Setnayan-owned music. Same posting flow as the prior single-SKU spec. **(2) Personal TikTok tier — ₱1,999/day:** **couple BYO TikTok via OAuth** (one-time OAuth handshake during purchase flow); videos auto-post to the couple's own TikTok handle; couple owns all videos + analytics + ad-revenue upside. **(3) Soft cap: 40 videos per day per booth** — protects Setnayan margin (compilation render + storage + per-clip face-lock processing scales with video count); booth dashboard shows a live counter; at 40 the operator sees a soft-warning ("You've captured your day's allotted 40 videos · keep recording with the overage add-on") and can either stop or buy overage. **(4) Overage SKU: ₱49 per +10 videos** (multi-purchase — operator can stack as many +10 blocks as they want at the venue without leaving the booth flow). **(5) Per-day multi-purchase for multi-day events** — Filipino weddings often span 2-3 days (prep + ceremony + reception each at a different venue); couple buys per-day Patiktok exactly like Panood Daily Broadcast (₱999 × 3 = ₱2,997 for the Setnayan-tier 3-day, ₱1,999 × 3 = ₱5,997 for the Personal-tier 3-day). **Sound selection mechanics from the prior spec preserved:** couple curates 2 trending sounds (primary + backup) at purchase time; printable QR for the operator dashboard; multi-performer face-lock; downloadable backup copy with Setnayan-owned music (for off-TikTok sharing). **External display + dual-view UX preserved** (split-screen / PIP for venues with monitors). | Three drivers. **First**, the prior single-SKU ₱2,499/booth/5hr model under-served couples with multi-day weddings (a 3-day event meant either buying multiple full stations or skipping the booth on most days) and over-served couples with single-event-day weddings (5 hours is more than most receptions need). Per-day pricing matches event reality and the per-day Panood pattern decided in the same session. **Second**, the dual-tier split by video-ownership resolves a long-standing tension in the original spec — some couples want the viral marketing upside of `@SetnayanWeddings` (Setnayan amplifies their wedding to the platform's audience for free), other couples want their own TikTok to be where the wedding content lives forever (and want the ad-revenue + analytics). Charging differently for these two ownership models reflects the real value difference: BYO TikTok means Setnayan loses platform-marketing upside, so the price is ~2× to compensate. **Third**, the 40-video soft cap is calibrated to typical Filipino-wedding guest counts (200 guests × ~20% participation rate ≈ 40 unique submitters per booth per day); the soft cap rather than a hard cap with ₱49/+10 overage protects margin on outlier high-engagement events without forcing couples to buy a whole second booth purchase. The ₱49 overage charm-pricing keeps the in-event upsell low-friction. **Tax-tier note:** Setnayan-tier ₱999/day nets ~70% margin under V1 tax tier; Personal-tier ₱1,999/day nets ~72% (higher % because the OAuth + per-couple TikTok adds ~₱0 marginal cost vs the Setnayan-handle posting); overage SKU at ₱49 nets ~80%. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0017_patiktok/0017_patiktok.md` (§ Pricing rewritten — old ₱2,499/booth/5hr table retired · new dual-tier per-day table inserted with the 4 SKU rows above · TikTok integration § rewritten to describe **two posting paths**: Setnayan-tier auto-post to `@SetnayanWeddings` (preserved from old spec) + Personal-tier OAuth-based auto-post to couple's own handle (new section) · sound-selection / multi-performer / external-display / downloadable-backup subsections preserved · soft-cap + overage subsection added · Coordinator workflow section updated to reference per-day multi-purchase · Anti-abuse rules table updated — the prior 500-submission-per-station-per-event cap is replaced by the 40-videos/day soft cap + overage); | 2026-05-16 | **V1 blended net margin lock at V1 tax tier — ~67-72% net across most SKUs · 90% gross margin (COGS ≤10%) achieved · 90% NET mathematically impossible under PH tax law · projected ~₱4M annual net profit at 1,000 events × ₱6K avg revenue.** Seventh 2026-05-16 row. Closes today's V1 SKU lock burst with a margin-discipline lock to prevent future scope drift toward "90% net margin" framing that's mathematically impossible under PH non-VAT V1 tax. **(1) V1 tax assumption locked:** Percentage Tax 3% (NIRC § 116 · annual gross ≤₱3M threshold) + Local Business Tax 1% (LBT — Manila / Makati rate) + Income Tax 25% (graduated table corporate rate post first ₱5M). Total tax wedge ~28-29% of gross revenue. **(2) Achievable net margin range:** ~67-72% across most V1 SKUs. **(3) Achievable gross margin range:** **~90% (COGS ≤10%)** — this is the "90% margin" headline that's accurate when properly labeled as **gross**, not net. **(4) Why 90% NET is impossible:** PH non-VAT tax wedge (~28-29%) + non-zero COGS (storage / compute / SMS / OAuth-API quotas) puts the theoretical max net margin at ~72% even with 100% gross margin SKUs. The headline "90% margin" claim only holds at gross. **(5) Annual net profit projection at V1 scale:** 1,000 events × ₱6,000 avg revenue per event = **₱6M annual gross**; minus 10% COGS = ₱5.4M gross profit; minus 28% tax wedge = **~₱4M annual net profit**. **(6) Worst-case tax tier (V1.5+ when annual gross crosses ₱3M VAT-registration threshold):** 12% VAT + 35% income tax (top bracket) puts the wedge at ~42-45%; net margin floats to ~52-57% across SKUs. **All SKUs remain profitable** even at worst-case tax tier — no V1 SKU is below break-even under V2 tax regime, so the upgrade path does not force re-pricing. **(7) Per-SKU net-margin snapshot at V1 tax tier:** Save-the-Date Video ₱99 = ~70% net · Monogram Hero ₱1,999 = ~70% net (Potrace ~₱0 cost / minimal R2 storage) · Live Schedule ₱999 = ~71% net · Panood Daily Broadcast ₱499 = ~67-70% net (broadcaster compute) · Panood Camera Sync ₱99/day = ~70% net · Panood Annual ₱2,999 = ~70-72% net · Panood Annual Plus ₱3,999 = ~70-72% net · Patiktok Setnayan ₱999/day = ~70% net · Patiktok Personal ₱1,999/day = ~72% net · Patiktok overage ₱49/+10 = ~80% net · all V1.5+ Papic SKUs land in the 65-72% net band per row 3 above. **(8) Disciplined revenue framing rule:** internal docs + investor materials + marketing copy must label margin claims explicitly as "gross" or "net"; the bare "90% margin" headline without qualifier is **retired** from V1 messaging because it conflates the two and creates expectation-management debt. | Three drivers. **First**, the V1 tax tier (non-VAT · ₱3M-gross threshold · 3% Percentage Tax) is a deliberate choice the corporate filing has committed to, not a stretch assumption — but it sets a mathematical ceiling on net margin that is lower than the colloquial "90% margin" framing in pre-launch decks would suggest. Locking the assumption now (rather than discovering it during BIR Form 1701Q quarterly filing) lets the revenue model + investor narrative be honest from launch. **Second**, locking the per-SKU net-margin snapshot at the V1 tax tier with the 5 SKU locks already decided today (Papic V1.5+ pricing · Panood per-day · Save-the-Date Video · Patiktok dual-tier) consolidates today's decision burst into one verifiable economic story — every SKU lock today rolls up to the ₱4M annual net projection at 1,000 events. The projection is a back-of-envelope but it is traceable to today's specific lock decisions, not aspirational marketing. **Third**, calling out the worst-case V2 tax tier (12% VAT + 35% income at the top corporate bracket) and showing the model is still profitable under that regime — net floats to 52-57% — locks in that V1 SKU prices do NOT need to be revised when Setnayan crosses the VAT-registration threshold. The upgrade path is "more taxes, less margin, but still profitable across the board" rather than "have to re-price the SKU table." | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `05_Financials/Cost_vs_Revenue_Analysis.xlsx` (margin tab to be regenerated next pricing-workbook pass with the new SKU rows from today's batch + the V1 tax tier formula assumption); `05_Financials/Pricing_Workbook_Set_Your_Prices.xlsx` (per-SKU net margin column to be regenerated with the V1 tax wedge); `05_Financials/Revenue_Projection_Model.xlsx` (annual scenarios updated to the ₱4M-at-1,000-events baseline projection); auto-memory: consider extending `project_setnayan.md` with a one-line note that V1 margin discipline is "90% gross / 67-72% net at V1 tax tier" so future sessions don't drift back to "90% net" framing. **`.docx` mirrors NOT regenerated** (pandoc unavailable). **No engineering implementation pending** — this is a margin-discipline / messaging lock, not a build item; the workbook regenerations are a Cowork bookkeeping task. **Marketplace commission row INTENTIONALLY EXCLUDED from this commit batch** (when that decision unlocks in a future Cowork pass, the marketplace SKUs + take-rate will be incorporated into the same margin model with their own tax-tier net-margin snapshot). **Sequencing note:** Seventh 2026-05-16 row · closes today's V1 SKU lock burst (rows 3-7 are the 5-item SKU framework lock; rows 1-2 were the earlier 0024 reframe + Monogram Hero PNG-to-SVG amendment). |

| 2026-05-16 | **Setnayan Pay convenience fee repriced 5.5%/6.5% → flat 5.0% on top of vendor price · Option B (vendor-absorbs-gateway) confirmed over Option A (Setnayan-absorbs-gateway) · supersedes the morning's 8th 2026-05-16 row.** Sixteenth 2026-05-16 row. Owner-ratified design target finalized — **3% net to Setnayan after all taxes at worst-case tax tier**. **(1) Math:** required gross = 3% ÷ (1 − tax_wedge) → V1 small-biz 28% wedge needs 4.17% gross · V2 VAT-registered 35% wedge needs 4.62% gross · extreme 40% wedge needs 5.00% gross. **5.0% flat is the minimum gross that holds the 3% net floor under every plausible tax scenario** with cushion for chargebacks / failed transactions / disbursement-fee absorption. **(2) Yields by tier at 5.0% flat:** V1 (28% wedge) → 3.60% net (1.67× the 2.16% operating breakeven); V2 realistic (35% wedge) → 3.25% net (1.50×); extreme worst (40% wedge) → 3.00% net (1.39×). **(3) Option B (vendor-absorbs-gateway) confirmed** over Option A (Setnayan-absorbs-gateway) because (a) Stripe Connect / Airbnb / Lazada Marketplace / every PH marketplace works this way so vendors expect it · (b) it insulates Setnayan from gateway rate risk forever (if Maya raises QR Ph from 1.5% → 2%, vendor absorbs not Setnayan) · (c) it lets the customer-facing headline stay at a clean flat 5.0% without rail-specific math at the cart · (d) Vendor Studio subscribers can be offered a gateway-absorbed perk in V1.5 as a subscription-conversion lever without disturbing V1 economics. Under Option A, Setnayan would have needed 6.21% gross to net 3% — bigger headline, more rail-rate risk, no upside. **(4) Annual revenue impact** vs the morning's 5.5%/6.5% lock at 500 paying couples × ₱300K avg booking through Setnayan Pay: −₱750K gross / −₱540K net per year — accepted because the 3% net target is achieved precisely and the round-number 5.0% headline strengthens marketing. **(5) Three rate epochs now in the decision log** within iteration 0034 itself: original 3% (≤ 2026-05-15, retired — below breakeven at every tax tier) · morning 5.5%/6.5% (2026-05-16 AM, retired — over-collected against the 3% net target) · evening flat 5.0% (2026-05-16 PM, this row, LIVE). **(6) Schema unchanged structurally:** `service_orders.fees_centavos` still derived as `subtotal × fee_bps_for_method / 10000`; `payment_method_config.setnayan_fee_bps` default 500 (was 550/650 dual-rate); per-method override capability retained for future rail-cost shocks. | Two drivers. **First, the morning's 5.5%/6.5% rate over-collected against the owner's actual 3% net design target.** The morning lock was tuned for a "safe profit per booking" intuition rather than a stated net target. Adds the outbound-disbursement half of the marketplace payment architecture, complementing the inbound Setnayan Pay flow locked yesterday (rows 16-17 of 2026-05-16). **(1) Three rails, three speeds, three costs:** **Intra-Maya** (vendor has Maya Bank account → instant + free + 24/7 for both vendor and Setnayan); **InstaPay** (Maya → any PH bank → < 1 min + 24/7 incl. weekends + ~₱10 bulk rate absorbed by Setnayan); **PESONet** (Maya → any PH bank → EOD same banking day (or T+1 weekends/holidays) + ~₱15 bulk rate absorbed by Setnayan). **(2) Default routing per payout type:** verified vendor immediate payout → InstaPay; coming_soon vendor 3-stage milestone → PESONet; any vendor on Maya Bank → intra-Maya regardless of payout type; payouts < ₱500 or > ₱500K (above InstaPay cap) → PESONet. **(3) Vendor override** in 0022 Vendor Dashboard payout preferences — verified vendors can downgrade default to PESONet for ₱5/payout rebate credit (Setnayan saves ₱5, vendor earns ₱5, both incentivized); coming_soon vendors can upgrade individual milestone to InstaPay by absorbing the ₱5 difference. **(4) Maya Bank vendor-recruiting pitch** — canonical copy "Get paid instantly, free, 24/7 — open a Maya Bank business account · Or get paid in under a minute to any PH bank, including weekends (InstaPay) · Standard payout settles end of business day (PESONet) — default for milestone releases." Surfaces on verification approval email + 0022 onboarding tour + payout-preferences settings. Strongest vendor-recruiting incentive in the payments architecture — every Maya Bank account opened means instant+free payouts for the vendor AND zero disbursement cost for Setnayan, forever. **(5) Schema (0034 § 6.9):** new `disbursement_batches` table (batch_id · generated_by_admin_id · rail enum (instapay/pesonet/mixed) · csv_r2_key · recipient_count · total_centavos · status enum (pending_upload/uploaded/partial_success/complete/failed) · maya_batch_reference · row_outcomes JSONB · timestamps); new columns on `vendor_payouts` (`rail` enum, `rail_chosen_by` enum, `batch_id` FK nullable, `status` enum widened to pending/batched/disbursed/failed/manual_reconciliation); two new indexes for batch-status queries. **(6) Failure handling:** if Maya rejects any row in a bulk batch (invalid account number, KYC mismatch, frozen account), that payout's status reverts to `pending` and rejoins next-day batch. Banned account variant shows the explanatory copy + appeal CTA in place of the upgrade banner. | Two drivers. **First, single-SKU = product confidence.** The 2026-05-16 2-tier model still read as a SaaS discount ladder ("we have a cheap option and a real option") rather than a confident product posture ("here's the product · ₱4,999"). The Apple iPhone playbook (one price per model · optional accessories not optional tiers) lands better in the wedding category where couples spend ₱200K–2M on the event itself — Setnayan looks more like a category-defining product and less like a subscription menu. The ₱2,499 Essentials tier was projected to under-perform vs Complete anyway (the savings math at ₱500/6-month-extra didn't anchor; most converters were projected to pick Complete), so retiring it removes a low-conversion SKU + simplifies the marketing surface + removes a "save face" branch that some couples were going to pick for budget reasons rather than fit reasons. Net revenue per Concierge customer is now uniformly ₱4,999 (was bimodal ₱2,499/₱4,999), which simplifies internal forecasting + makes the pricing-page anchor (₱25K coordinator vs ₱4,999 Concierge) cleaner without the ₱2,499 mid-anchor cluttering the comparison. **Second, the 3-day trial + account-level cap + tiered enforcement framework closes a real multi-account abuse vector** the owner identified. The 2026-05-16 7-day per-event preview model had two known holes: (a) one couple creating Event A, exhausting trial, creating Event B on the same account for another trial; (b) one person creating Account A, exhausting trial, creating Account B with a near-identical wedding profile for another trial. Hole (a) closes mechanically with the per-account cap (`users.concierge_trial_used_at`). Hole (b) requires similarity detection — the on-trial-start check + admin review queue + tiered enforcement framework. The tiered enforcement (warn → trial-ban → full-ban) is more forgiving than a single-strike auto-ban because (i) similarity hits include genuine false positives (sibling couples planning at the same venue · wedding-planner accounts managing multiple clients · same venue different couples on different dates) which need admin judgment, and (ii) the progressive penalty creates a forgiveness lane on first offense that reduces customer-support load from legit users wrongly hit on the first flag. Filipino-market consideration: wedding-coordinator accounts and multi-client agencies are a legit segment that will pattern-match on venue/date overlap with their own clients — these are NOT abuse and need admin-confirmable clearing on first flag. The tiered model gives the platform room to learn without permanently banning legitimate edge cases. **Trial duration 7 → 3 days drivers:** (a) 3 days is enough to walk through the 9-step roadmap and see the Concierge value (each step is ~5-10 minutes for an engaged couple); (b) shorter trial reduces account-creation incentive for trial-cycling (3 days of free access is less "worth the abuse effort" than 7 days); (c) the ₱4,999 sticker is now anchored against "a focused 72-hour preview" rather than "a leisurely week" — better matches the premium-product feel that supports the single-SKU framing. **Risk accepted:** lower trial → buy conversion than the 7-day model would have produced. Mitigated by (i) the 9-step roadmap being demonstrably valuable in the first hour (couples see deadline alerts + vendor picks within Step 1-2), (ii) the choice card still offering DIY-free as the no-cost option for couples who aren't ready, (iii) the human-coordinator anchor still doing the heavy lifting on pricing-page conversion. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry) · iteration table row #0016 (rewritten to single-SKU + 3-day trial + tiered enforcement framing); | 2026-05-17 | **Setnayan Concierge access switched from fixed-12-months to wedding-anchored with a 24-month cap — fixes the long-engagement edge case where a couple with a 3-year engagement was losing access 24 months before their wedding day.** Third 2026-05-17 row. Owner-surfaced edge-case fix: under the prior fixed-12-month spec, a couple setting their wedding 3 years out and paying ₱4,999 would have lost Concierge 24 months before they actually needed it — a bad customer experience that risked refund disputes and brand damage. **(1) New access-duration formula:** `concierge_expires_at = LEAST(GREATEST(wedding_date + INTERVAL '30 days', activation_date + INTERVAL '12 months'), activation_date + INTERVAL '24 months')`. **(2) Guarantees:** every paying couple gets a **floor of 12 months** of access from activation (so couples with no date yet OR very-soon weddings still get a full year), and a **ceiling of 24 months** from activation (caps margin exposure on extreme long engagements). **(3) Sweet-spot ranges:** wedding 3 months out → 12 months access (12-month floor wins · 9 months post-wedding tail) · wedding 8 months out → 12 months (floor wins) · wedding 12 months out → 12.5 months (wedding+30 wins) · wedding 18 months out → 18.5 months (wedding+30) · wedding 24 months out → 24 months (cap) · wedding 36 months out → 24 months (cap · couple sees 24-month advisory). **(4) NULL wedding_date handling:** at activation, if `events.wedding_date IS NULL` (typical because the choice card per 0000 § 2.5a defers date entry to Concierge Step 1 OR Profile), `expires_at` defaults to `activation_date + INTERVAL '12 months'`. When `wedding_date` is later set/updated, expires_at recomputes per the formula above — but **only extends, never shrinks**. **(5) Wedding-date update behavior:** if couple updates `wedding_date` to a later date after activation, `concierge_expires_at` extends to the new wedding+30 (up to the 24-month cap). If couple updates to an earlier date, expires_at STAYS at the original value (they already paid for that runway; no shrinkage). **(6) Long-engagement advisory:** when `wedding_date` is set or updated to > 24 months from `concierge_activated_at`, a one-time in-app + email advisory surfaces: *"Your wedding is more than 24 months away. Setnayan Concierge covers up to 24 months from your purchase date — you'll lose access ~{N} months before your wedding. We recommend renewing closer to your wedding for full coverage."* Stamp a `concierge_long_engagement_advised_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column on `events` to prevent re-fire on subsequent date updates. **(7) Schema:** the existing `events.concierge_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column from the 2026-05-17 lock is unchanged structurally — just the formula that populates it changes; new column `events.concierge_long_engagement_advised_at TIMESTAMPTZ` added for the advisory de-dup. **(8) Server-action update:** `activate_concierge(event_id, order_id)` computes `expires_at` per the formula at activation time using whatever `wedding_date` value is present (NULL → defaults to activation+12mo). New server action `recompute_concierge_expiry(event_id)` fires from the `events.wedding_date` update trigger (or app-layer hook) — recomputes per the formula + applies the extend-only rule + triggers the advisory if conditions met. **(9) Daily expiry sweep unchanged** — still flips status to `'expired'` when `expires_at < NOW()`. **(10) Refund/dispute exposure capped** — under the prior model, a couple paying ₱4,999 with a 36-month engagement and losing access at month 12 had a strong "I was misled" case; under the new model the worst-case is a couple with a >24-month engagement, and they see the advisory at purchase/date-entry, so they make an informed choice. | Two drivers. **First, the prior fixed-12-months model created a real product-market mismatch for long engagements.** Filipino couples plan 6–24 months out modally (per the locked planning-runway assumptions in iteration 0016 § 1), but a non-trivial tail (anniversary-fresh engagements · couples who got engaged years before they could afford the wedding · couples coordinating with overseas family that need long lead times) plans 24–48 months out. Under the prior model these couples paid ₱4,999 and lost access well before the wedding — the value proposition collapsed precisely when it mattered most. The wedding-anchored formula matches the actual job-to-be-done ("help us plan THIS wedding") without breaking the simple single-SKU pricing model. **Second, the 24-month cap protects Setnayan's per-event economics.** A truly unbounded wedding-anchored model (e.g., access until wedding_date + 30 days with no cap) would mean a 5-year-engagement couple gets 5 years of Concierge for ₱4,999 — that's an effective rate of ₱83/month, well below the per-customer economics this SKU was sized for (~₱416/month over 12 months). Capping at 24 months means the worst-case effective rate is ~₱208/month, still healthy margin, and the affected customer segment (>24-month engagements) is small. The advisory + renewal-encouragement copy turns the cap from a hidden gotcha into a transparent renewal hook. **Third, the 12-month floor protects the short-engagement / no-date-yet case** — couples who buy Concierge before setting a wedding date OR with very-soon weddings still get a guaranteed full year of access including post-wedding planning tail, matching the brand promise that "Access doesn't end at the wedding date." **Filipino-market consideration:** the long-engagement-advisory copy will be in EN-primary luxurious-Filipino-modern voice (per COWORK.md line 74) and will not penalize couples who got engaged years in advance — it surfaces as a friendly "heads-up" not a "you bought wrong" guilt-trip. **Extend-only rule on date changes** is the customer-fair default — a couple who postpones their wedding deserves more runway; | 2026-05-17 | **Event date-change flow with booked vendors — multi-party state machine locked.** Customer-facing date edits route through a confirmation gate that triggers only when the event has **≥1 confirmed vendor** (cart/draft don't count toward the threshold; mediation-state vendors do). The gate is a single modal with the affected-vendor list + a required reason field (min 30 chars). On submit: schedule check runs against each vendor's calendar; couple sees one of two messages — *"Your schedule change is available for all vendors. Waiting for their confirmation."* OR *"Your schedule change is available for X vendors but conflicts for Y vendors. We cannot apply this change until all vendors accept."* Pending state freezes everything (original date holds on both sides, no further date attempts by couple, payments paused, vendor slots locked from re-allocation). Vendor decline does NOT auto-fail the request — it routes the booking into the existing customer↔vendor chat thread (per the customer-initiates-chat rule), which gains a **structured action card** with Propose alternate / Accept this date / Cancel booking / Escalate to support buttons. Free-text agreements in chat are not load-bearing — only the action cards trigger state transitions, otherwise bookings sit frozen indefinitely. Timeouts both ways: vendor ghost past **48 hr** → auto-escalate to admin mediation tier (0023 Disputes Handler joins the thread, same pattern as the force-majeure flow in 0019 + the refund/dispute menu in iteration 0021 § 2.2); couple ghost past **72 hr** of active chat negotiation → request auto-cancels and event reverts to original date. Mediation outcomes (mediator selects from a fixed enum, no free-text resolutions): vendor reconsiders, couple stays on original date, vendor swap, full refund + cancellation of that vendor only, reschedule-fee compromise. Race condition: if a vendor backs out *during* an active date-change negotiation and that drops the confirmed-vendor count to zero, the in-flight negotiation auto-resolves and the couple is free to apply the change immediately. When the count transitions ≥1 → 0 for any reason (last vendor backs out, mediation cancels everyone, all vendors released), a passive "All vendors have been released — you can now change your event date freely" banner surfaces on the dashboard Home; dismisses on first date-edit attempt or after 14 days. Reschedule fees: vendors enter their per-window policy at onboarding (0006); V1 leaves fee enforcement as a manual mediator action (auto-debit lands in 0034 Phase 2). Hard cap of **2 date changes** per event lifecycle; third attempt is gated behind admin override via 0029 help center. Locked into iteration 0021 § 10 (new section). | Wedding-date changes are emotionally and contractually high-stakes — Filipino weddings involve venue deposits, vendor schedules booked 8–12 months out, and family travel logistics. A naive "edit and save" date field would either lock couples out of legitimate changes (force majeure, family emergency, venue issue) or break vendor trust by moving the date without their input. Routing both sides through structured negotiation surfaces (modal → schedule check → vendor confirm → chat with action cards → admin mediation) preserves vendor agency without leaving couples stranded, captures a reason for every change (audit trail + vendor empathy + admin dispute pattern detection), and reuses existing chat + force-majeure mediation infrastructure rather than building a parallel surface. Affects iterations: 0021 (couple dashboard — canonical spec, new § 10), 0006 (vendor side — receives the request action card + reschedule policy capture), 0019 (chat infrastructure — must support structured/interactive action cards as a first-class message type), 0023 (admin console — mediation tier + dispute ticket reuse), 0034 (payment freeze during pending state · auto-debit of reschedule fees deferred to Phase 2). |
| 2026-05-17 | **App Store hero-CTA 5-state model locked — Add · Request Sent · Launch · Blocked · Expired — plus event-switcher expired-rightmost sort.** Owner directive after the Panood pilot ship: replace the binary "Choose plan" / "Open setup" CTA with five explicit states the App Store-style hero button cycles through. **(1) Add** — no active order against any feature SKU; opens the Choose Plan sheet. **(2) Request Sent** — couple has submitted an order but admin hasn't confirmed payment (`orders.status ∈ {'submitted','awaiting_payment'}`); button is a chip-style link to `/dashboard/[eventId]/orders/[orderPublicId]` so the couple can see the reference code + payment status. **(3) Launch** — feature is paid/fulfilled (`orders.status ∈ {'paid','fulfilled'}`); button links to the per-feature setup surface (for Panood: `/setup`; for Mood Board: the feature itself; for vendor services: the booking workspace). **(4) Blocked** — admin policy disables the feature for this account type (or per-event override applies); button is a disabled chip with the admin block-reason as the tooltip. **(5) Expired** — event passed its **wedding_date + 90 day** grace cutoff (OR is admin-archived); button is a disabled chip explaining the event ended. Resolution precedence: **expired > blocked > launch > request_sent > add**. The hero `statusPill` mirrors the state (Active on this event / Pending review / Unavailable / Event ended / Web V1 fallback for add). The same model applies to vendor service detail pages — same resolver, accountType=vendor_certified for vendor-side rendering. **Event switcher sort change:** active events first (primary → date-asc, unchanged inside the active group), then expired events pushed to the end with **date-desc** so the oldest-expired event lands at the rightmost / final slot ("oldest expired is the farthest" per owner directive). Archived events stay filtered out of the switcher per existing behavior — V1 keeps that surface, but the expired-by-date path now sorts cleanly to the right without dropping events. **Schema:** new `public.feature_policy(feature_key PK, enabled_for_couples, enabled_for_vendors_coming_soon, enabled_for_vendors_certified, block_reason_* TEXT, updated_by_admin_id, created_at, updated_at)` + `public.event_feature_policy_override(event_id+feature_key PK, enabled, reason, set_by_admin_id, set_at)` — mirrors the per-account-type policy primitive locked earlier today for payment methods. RLS: public read on feature_policy (state must be readable to render the CTA); per-event override scoped to `current_event_ids()` for couples + open to admins. Admin-only write on both. Seed enables all 9 add-on launcher keys for couples; vendors_coming_soon gated off by default except `orders` (vendor side reads orders too). **No admin UI in this PR** — admins flip flags via direct DB until the 0023 Feature Policy panel ships in a fan-out PR. | Two drivers. **First, the binary owned/not-owned CTA hid three important states the couple needed to see.** Request Sent in particular was invisible — a couple who submitted an order via apply-then-pay would land back on the detail page with no signal that anything was in flight, which trains "I should re-submit" behavior that costs admins reconciliation time. Surfacing the reference code in the chip closes the loop. Blocked is the existing payment-options policy primitive applied to features — admins already have per-account-type levers for payment rails (locked earlier today); the same primitive now covers feature visibility so a vendor in coming_soon state doesn't get pitched Same-Day Edit and a couple under abuse review doesn't see a buyable Concierge tile. | 2026-05-17 | **Event venue-change flow — reuses the date-change state machine with a coverage-check substitution.** Same multi-party pattern as the § 10 date-change flow (gate triggered by ≥1 confirmed vendor · required reason field · pending-state freeze across all surfaces including the public landing page · 48 hr vendor response window · 72 hr couple chat timeout · chat negotiation via structured action cards · admin mediation tier · 2-changes cap · door-reopened banner). Customer-facing messaging adapts accordingly: *"Your venue change is available for all vendors. Waiting for their confirmation."* OR *"Your venue change is available for X vendors but is in conflict for Y vendors. We cannot apply this change until all vendors accept."* **(2)** the per-vendor fee field is a **relocation fee** (travel cost · equipment shipping · venue-specific insurance riders) rather than a reschedule fee, surfaced from vendor onboarding (0006) the same way. **Auto-accept policy (NEW · venue-only):** vendors set a service-area radius at onboarding (e.g., "auto-accept any venue within 50 km of Manila"); venues inside the radius skip the vendor confirmation card entirely and the booking auto-transitions. Venues outside the radius (or vendors who opted out of auto-accept) get the standard card. Cuts negotiation volume materially for short-distance venue swaps (e.g., changing from one Tagaytay venue to another). Mediation outcome enum mirrors § 10.6 with venue-specific labels: vendor reconsiders → service new venue · couple stays at original venue · vendor swap · refund + cancellation · relocation-fee compromise. A naive "edit and save" venue field strands vendors who can't service the new location (e.g., catering vendor with no permit for the new municipality, lights & sound with travel constraints, florist outside service area). Reusing the § 10 state machine with a coverage-check substitution keeps engineering scope tight (same UI · same state transitions · same admin tooling) — only the vendor-side check differs. Auto-accept radius cuts the operational tax on the common case (short-distance moves) where vendor disruption is minimal.
